description: The standard approach to responsible AI is fundamentally broken. In the age of generative AI, it’s too slow, too vague, and too hard to communicate. That’s because this focus allows them to apply a novel, rapidly implementable approach that works for everything from narrow AI to governing AI agents. The Ethical Nightmare Challenge asks three questions: 1) What are the ethical nightmares of your organization as they pertain to AI? 2) What resources will you build to avoid those nightmares? 3) How will you train your people to use those resources effectively?

description: Many managers are criticized for showing leniency in performance reviews for low performers. But new research finds that may actually be a rational response to a costly problem: employee retaliation. When negative evaluations trigger gossip, slowdowns, or even sabotage, the financial and cultural damage can outweigh the benefits of strict enforcement. Using a theoretical model and real-world examples, the study shows that tying pay tightly to performance improves measurement but increases backlash risk, especially for long-term employees. Firms may be better off emphasizing bonuses for top performance, overlooking minor shortfalls, and separating developmental feedback from compensation to preserve both productivity and workplace harmony.
title: Why Leaders Should Let Minor Mistakes Slide
